summary: Clean, plan-based win on CPI day. Your pre-market said you wanted the data high hit while price sat inside 4hr bullish gaps, and you went long after the CPI flush retraced into OTE, the 1hr rejection block and a 5min FVG, then rode it through the data high into the D-OPEN. You took profit at the D-OPEN after a 1min internal SMT instead of holding for PDH. That was a reasonable call, but your own note says 'my mind kept messing w me thinking the move would fully go back to entry for BE', so the exit came from fear of giving it back, not from a level in your plan. After you closed, price rejected from about 28,090 and fell to about 27,866 by 10:40, so taking profit at the D-OPEN was the better result today. The miss today is the morning check-in: nothing was filed before 9:30 AM ET, so there's no risk-settings screenshot on record for a CPI day.
trade: Long · NY-AM · XFA · Trailed out W · entry ≈ 27,768.75 (around 9:45 AM ET) · stop ≈ 27,644.75 at the 1min internal low that swept (≈124 pts) · RR tool target ≈ 28,036 (≈2.1R), closed around the D-OPEN ≈ 28,060 · DOL data high (hit) / PDH ≈ 28,118 (not reached).
rule: Tomorrow, write your exit plan in the pre-market box before 9:30: which level you take partials at and what makes you hold for the final DOL. Then only exit on that rule, not on the feeling that price will come back to your entry.

screenshots.label: Execution 1 · 1min NQ (10:40 AM)
screenshots.feedback: The RR tool shows entry at about 27,768.75 with the stop at about 27,644.75, just under the 0.705–0.786 OTE band and the swept 1min internal low, and the target box tops out around 28,036. Price ran through the data high (about 28,000) and wicked to about 28,090 just after 10:00, then sold off to 27,866 by 10:40. Your notes on the chart match Notion. The stop sits above the NY AM low (about 27,620), so a deeper sweep of that low would have stopped you out before the move. Worth knowing when you size it.

screenshots.label: TimeFrame 1 · 4hr NQ + 15min ES (9:29 AM)
screenshots.feedback: The 4hr shows NQ bouncing off the Nov 6 lows back toward PD-H (about 28,120), with PD-EQ around 27,450 and PD-L around 26,800. That supports the long bias and PDH as the bigger DOL. ES on the 15min had already dumped below its Asia and London lows into the 10:00 line.

screenshots.label: TimeFrame 2 · 15min NQ + ES (9:31 AM)
screenshots.feedback: The CPI candle at 8:30 swept down to about 27,590 and NQ was around 27,689 at 9:31, under the Asia low, the London low and the D-OPEN (about 28,075). Marking the NY AM high and low and the D-OPEN before the open is what let you spot the D-OPEN rejection later. Good prep.
